verdict.rationale: Ghostty documents a built-in AppleScript dictionary for scripting windows, tabs, terminals, layouts, and input events, plus Apple Shortcuts support. That gives a first-party way to script a multi-window, tab, and split workspace launched in one command. However, it is macOS-only, and nothing shows a declarative config-based way to define startup sessions or layouts; per-key CLI flags only set options, not layouts. Missing for 10: declarative layout/session definitions in config, a Linux scripting equivalent, worked examples or independent hands-on corroboration of scripted workspace launch.
